newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's CRT shares transferred for 681 mln reais.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's CRT shares transferred for 681 mln reais.

text.p: The sale of a 35-percent stake in state-owned telecom CRT was formally concluded with the transfer of shares to a Brazilian-Spanish consortium for 681 million reais, officials said.

Federal telecom Telebras said in a notice to Brazil's stock markets that 262,352,653 voting common of CRT were transferred to the group including Brazil's RBS Participacoes and Spain's Telefonica de Espana.
While most of the shares sold to the consortium were owned by Rio Grande do Sul state, 43,835,676 or a roughly five-percent stake were owned by Telebras.

The RBS-Telefonica group on December 17 cast the winning bid for the 35-percent stake in CRT, known formally as Companhia Riograndense de Telecomunicacoes, but the transfer was blocked by a court injunction shortly after the auction.
The injunction, sought by the Workers Party (PT) on grounds the state had used the shares to back a loan and thus did not own them, was lifted last week, clearing the way for the transfer.
The winning consortium also included Telefonica units Telefonica de Argentina and CTC of Chile as well as Citicorp.

The sale of the CRT shares, bought for almost 54.8 percent more than the base price, was closely watched by the market because it represented the first opening of Brazil's telecoms sector to private capital.

Brazil plans next year to start privatizing its massive telecommunications sector, first by offering cellular telephone concessions then moving to break-up and sell off Telebras, Latin America's largest telecom.
